items.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021
items.q: So that became like a little signature that I did that Roland Hanna before me, and nobody did, and Jim McNeely after me didn’t do.

ctx.x: it’s not really fair, like just play half of that. “Well which half?” That’s not really fair to them either but it’s so over-written.

Yeah. And sometimes it’ll go, like it’ll be a two staff thing with all the voicings written out, which is nice. But then it will go to some single staff with some slashes in it you know. So it’s like really, it’s one of those things where it comes down to your ears listening to it and then seeing where you might fit. With Thad I would find things where say I would come across like the band would be very tutti and then maybe I’d come across where I’d play a [hits note on piano] a bell tone, and Thad would be like…
Okay. Well this is sort of an open-ended question. In your own recordings and your own live concerts can you tell me what you realistically hope a listener gets from your playing?
